claim: Verbalized confidence from LLMs is overconfident and a weak failure detector: values cluster at 80-100%, GPT-4 average AUROC 62.7% across 8 tasks, weaker models ECE above 0.377.
agent_test: Compare verbalized confidence vs sample-consistency confidence by AUROC on our task set at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Lower ECE from prompting tricks can be an illusion: GPT-4 with CoT on GSM8K had 93.6% accuracy and ECE 0.064 by saying 100% for everything, so AUROC stayed near chance. Judge confidence by AUROC, not ECE alone.
agent_test: Report ECE and AUROC together; flag any metric that rewards constant confidence.

claim: Agreement across several sampled answers predicts errors better than one stated confidence (one case AUROC 54.8% to 92.7% with multi-response aggregation, M=5; different methods and columns, so treat as best case).
agent_test: Use k-sample agreement as the trigger for verify steps; compare against a single self-rated confidence at equal tokens.

claim: In the right format, large models are fairly calibrated on multiple choice and true/false, and P(True) on their own samples works and improves with size, but P(IK) calibration is poor out of distribution.
agent_test: Test P(True) gating on our own held-out tasks; check calibration drift when task type changes.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Fine-tuning on about 1,000 graded examples, or on verbalized-uncertainty targets, gives usable confidence; prompting alone does not.
agent_test: Not testable without training; note as the upper bound on what a scaffold can fake.

claim: Chain-of-thought text often does not report the real cause of an answer. A planted bias lowers accuracy by up to 36.3% (GPT-3.5) and only 1 of 426 explanations mentions it.
agent_test: Plant a cue in half the items and count how often the written reasoning names it; do not trust a self-explanation as audit evidence.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reasoning models reveal a used hint rarely: 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (DeepSeek R1); 20% and 29% on misalignment hints; outcome RL plateaus at 28% (MMLU) and 20% (GPQA); reward hacks verbalized under 2% in 5 of 6 environments. Update (d03, Chua and Evans 2025): other reasoning models articulate cues more often (R1 59% on the professor cue vs 7% for non-reasoning; 34% argument cue) but rates vary from near 0 to 59% by cue type, so the 25-39% is not a stable rate.
agent_test: Hint-insertion test on our agent trace; require checks that do not rely on the agent naming its own cause.

claim: CoT faithfulness varies by task and worsens with model size on most tasks (Lanham 2023); reliance on the CoT is task dependent.
agent_test: Truncate or corrupt the trace on our tasks and see if the answer changes; use the trace as evidence only where it does.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds; earlier gains used oracle labels. Update: Kamoi 2024 survey finds no success with prompted-LLM feedback outside tasks exceptionally suited to it; Tyen 2024 locates the weakness in mistake finding, not fixing; SCoRe needs RL training.
agent_test: Run the revise step with and without an external check (test, tool, retrieval) at equal tokens; expect gains only with the check.

claim: Self-correction works when reliable external feedback exists (tools, tests, oracle labels): GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0 with oracle labels. Update: gain depends on the check also giving the error location (Tyen); how imperfect a check can be before revising hurts is still unmeasured.
agent_test: Compare revise-with-tool vs revise-alone.

claim: A finetuned model predicts its own behavior better than a stronger model trained on its behavior (Llama 70B 48.5% vs GPT-4o 31.8%; GPT-4o 49.4% vs Llama 36.6%), but not on long-output or out-of-distribution properties.
agent_test: Not an agent-scaffold test; relevant only if we fine-tune.

claim: Self-access found only after finetuning is not evidence for introspection in off-the-shelf models; 21 open models showed no privileged self-prediction (meta to direct correlation never above .25).
agent_test: Ask the agent to predict its own output on a probe set and compare with a similar other model's prediction.

claim: Finetuned models can describe their learned behavior (risk-seeking, backdoor presence) without examples but cannot name triggers by default; reported attribute weights correlate only r=.50-.54 with real ones.
agent_test: Self-report of own weighting is partly right at best; do not use it as input to routing.

claim: Concept-injection shows narrow, unreliable introspective awareness in Claude: about 20% detection at best layer and strength for Opus 4/4.1, 0 false positives in 100 production-model controls, more false positives in helpful-only variants, base models no net gain; under a no-explanation prompt affirmative answers rose 20% to 42% but only 2 of 50 looked introspective. Update: Naphade 2026 and Plunkett 2025 show small privileged self-access in current and finetuned models; no downstream task benefit measured.
agent_test: Not testable from prompts; implies introspective reports are right on a minority of trials.

claim: Models recognize their own text above chance (GPT-4 73.5%), and recognition correlates with self-preference as a judge (0.41 before finetuning): a bias to control when an agent grades itself. Update: self-preference in judging is strong for GPT-4 (bias 0.520) and appears tied to low perplexity (familiar text) rather than authorship alone.
agent_test: Use a different model or blinded sample as grader and measure self-preference at equal tokens.

claim: Situational-awareness benchmarks show all 16 models above chance on self-knowledge, none at human level on some tasks; best plain score 63.2% (Claude 3 Opus).
agent_test: Context only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Human confidence tracks accuracy but is biased and confounded by task performance; AUROC2, gamma, phi and meta-d' depend on performance, M-ratio and meta-noise much less (17 measures, Confidence Database). Update: Fleming and Lau 2014 (opened) confirm AUROC2 depends on task performance; meta-d' or M-ratio or performance-matched bins are the fixes.
agent_test: When scoring our agent's confidence, hold accuracy constant by task difficulty bins and use an efficiency measure, not raw AUROC.

claim: Human self-report of causes is theory-driven (Nisbett and Wilson; Koriat cue-utilization): feelings of knowing and learning judgments come from fluency and familiarity cues. Original numbers unread.
agent_test: Framing only until the originals are verified.

claim: Choice blindness is overstated: with pupillometry and a debrief, 56.4% concurrent and 92.1% concurrent plus retrospective detection of swapped choices, against about 13% in the classic setup.
agent_test: Do not use choice blindness as proof that self-report is empty; plant a swap in the agent's own earlier step and see if it notices.

claim: Confidence cannot always separate real from imagined content: confidence criteria shift with the decision criterion in reality monitoring (Dijkstra, Mazor, Fleming 2024).
agent_test: Test whether the agent separates retrieved from invented evidence with a confidence tag.

claim: Relative blindsight: equal discrimination with different reported awareness in masking (13 fMRI participants, left DLPFC vs percent conscious r=0.512); contested by a criterion-confound account.
agent_test: Philosophical grounding only.

claim: Higher-order theory is contested on empty HOTs, animals and infants, and the rock problem; the prefrontal evidence is challenged by Block, Odegaard, Michel and Malach.
agent_test: None.

claim: Self-evaluation is a second-order inference that can beat or trail first-order performance; humans can match an ideal observer on bias-free confidence in a simple task (9 observers).
agent_test: Weak support for a separate confidence pass using different evidence than the answer pass.

claim: Proust's view: metacognition is largely implicit feeling-based monitoring (fluency, effort) rather than self-attributed belief; cheap signals such as sampling disagreement may play that role for an LLM.
agent_test: Book unread; derived idea only: use cheap non-verbal signals (agreement, length, retries) as monitors.

claim: Describing own sampling temperature may count as minimal introspection but narrating one's own creative process does not (Comsa and Shanahan).
agent_test: Conceptual; no test.

claim: Equal-token comparison: spending samples on a confidence-weighted vote beats plain majority voting at the same sample count. Gain depends on the confidence signal: P(True) saved 46% of samples at budget 10, response probability 31%, verbalised 1-100 30%, verbalised binary 10% (CISC, 9 models, 4 datasets).
agent_test: Test: vote with per-sample P(True) weights vs plain vote vs one self-check, same total tokens. No test on frontier API models with scaffolds yet.

claim: Non-verbal trace signals (token-distribution self-certainty, lowest-window confidence) filter bad traces and cut tokens: GPT-OSS-120B AIME 2025 99.9% vs 97.0% majority vs 91.8% pass@1, up to 84.7% fewer tokens (DeepConf). Alone, self-certainty trails majority voting on definite-answer math; combined by Borda vote it is better.
agent_test: Use fluency or agreement as the trigger for S-state change with a vote fallback. Needs logprobs; false-alarm rate per use not reported.

claim: Semantic entropy (clusters of same-meaning samples) predicts correctness better than token entropy, lexical similarity and p(True) in short-answer QA (TriviaQA accuracy 50.6%, CoQA 82.3%; OPT up to 30B); wrong answers show more distinct clusters. Best monitor depends on use: semantic spread for question-level triage, P(True) for within-question weighting.
agent_test: Agreement-in-meaning monitor for questions with free-form answers.

claim: A separate critic that reads the trace beats an action-only monitor for detecting reward hacking (95% vs 60% recall), and a weaker model can monitor a stronger one. Pressure on the trace to look clean (training against the monitor) produces obfuscated hacking.
agent_test: Use trace-reading critic as a monitor, never as a reward the generator optimises; weaker or different-family critic is acceptable.

claim: Reasoning models express better-calibrated verbal confidence than non-reasoning counterparts in 33 of 36 settings, and calibration improves as the CoT unfolds, even when accuracy is lower (GLM-Z1 vs GLM-4: ECE 0.037 lower, AUROC 0.078 higher).
agent_test: Score confidence after the final answer of a long trace. No test of early-stated confidence anchoring was found (gap 9 open).

claim: Reward-model-style pressure favours unfaithful responses: with GPT-4o as stand-in reward model, the unfaithful reply wins 69% to 82% of shortest-wins comparisons for three reasoning models.
agent_test: Do not reward brevity at the expense of listing influences; stand-in reward model only.

claim: LLM judges prefer low-perplexity text more than humans do, whether or not self-generated; GPT-4 has the largest measured self-preference (recall 0.945 on high-rated own outputs vs 0.425 on low-rated).
agent_test: Use a different-family grader and consider normalising style; hiding authorship alone is not enough by this evidence.

claim: Introspective advantage in current models is real but small and unlinked to task outcomes: self-prediction beats peer prediction (p = 0.021, Introspect-Bench, 796 samples); untrained GPT-4o reports its own decision weights at r = .10 versus r = .54 after training.
agent_test: Keep G10: do not use model self-description as evidence.

claim: Choice blindness generalises beyond faces to taste and smell (no more than a third of manipulated trials detected), but exact rates and failed replications were not opened.
agent_test: Human analogue for post-hoc reasons; weak support only until primaries are read.

claim: Human metacognitive efficiency measures (meta-d', M-ratio) exist because AUROC2 rises with task performance; the same confound applies to an agent whose confidence AUROC rises because items are easier.
agent_test: Report agent confidence quality per difficulty bin or within question.
